subject: Control sampling & evidence prioritization — decision request
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Jan 2028 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Control sampling & evidence prioritization — request for decision

Team —

We need to lock down the sampling approach and evidence priorities for Acme Financial's upcoming combined ISO/FedRAMP intake. Auditor kickoff is next week (Jan 31). High-level asks from Acme: sample artifacts for ISO 27001 Annex A mappings, FedRAMP Moderate-equivalent control evidence for cloud boundary controls, and SOC 2 bridging notes where available.

Quick questions I want a short decision on by EOD today so we can reply to the auditor:

- Scope: do we include both hosted API (multi-tenant) and dedicated clusters used by Acme? (my recommendation: include only Dedicated capacity tied to their org id and the control boundary we previously agreed)
- Sampling window: 90 days vs 365 days for system logs and change control artifacts?
- Evidence types: prefer system exports/logs + IAM config exports over screenshots. Are there controls where screenshots are unavoidable?
- Sampling size: per-control sample (n=5) vs risk-weighted (n=3 high, n=1 medium)?

Attached is the evidence_index_template.csv — fill the first tab with candidate artifacts you think are highest priority to collect if you agree with the dedicated-only scope. Also flag owners.

If we can’t converge today, I’ll propose a compromise reply to the auditor asking for clarification on their minimum sampling expectations.

Thanks —
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Security & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: evidence_index_template.csv (CSV stub; columns: control_id, evidence_type, owner, file_stub, retention_window)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Jan 2028 10:14:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Control sampling & evidence prioritization — request for decision

Sean —

Agree with dedicated-only scope for Acme; scoping hosted API would expand control surface and slow the intake. Proposed decisions below:

- Scope: Dedicated instances only (include associated control plane interactions such as routing, user provisioning for that org id).
- Sampling window: use 90 days for operational logs (syslogs, API access logs) and 365 days for change-control artifacts (PRs, change tickets) and evidence of ongoing monitoring — this maps well to ISO evidence expectations and FedRAMP tendency to want longer retention for configuration management.
- Evidence types: prioritize exports (CSV/JSON), audit logs, KMS rotation records, IaC commit history, and policy-as-code diffs. Only use screenshots for UI-only items where an export isn’t available (rare).
- Sampling size: risk-weighted: 5 samples for high-critical controls (authentication, key management, tenant isolation), 3 for medium, 1 for low. For FedRAMP high-severity controls we should aim for n=7 where feasible.

Action items I suggest:
1) Jonas — populate evidence_index_template.csv for the top-12 controls (I put tentative control ids in column A).
2) Olga — confirm KMS and key rotation artifacts availability and retention window; identify owner(s).
3) Sean — draft auditor reply with scope/samples + ask for their minimal acceptable n per control so we can adjust.

I’ll also append a quick mapping: ISO Annex A -> FedRAMP control families -> our internal control ids to the spreadsheet so auditors can see the alignment.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Clara Holt <clara@acme-fin.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Security Intake <security-intake@acme-fin.com>, Auditor Team <audits@cyberproof.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Jan 2028 14:03:10 -0500
Subject: Re: Control sampling & evidence prioritization — Acme information request

Hi Sean / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick coordination. A couple clarifying items from Acme’s side to help the audit team plan:

- Scope confirmation: we accept dedicated-only but need the list of specific hostnames/cluster IDs and agent versions in scope by EOD Jan 25.
- Sampling expectations: our auditors typically expect 90-day windows for log evidence but require 12 months for change-control where the control maps to configuration management. If you can provide both 90d and 12mo exports where feasible that will be ideal.
- Evidence format: CSV/JSON exports are preferred. If a system only exposes a UI, a time-stamped screenshot is acceptable but please include a signed attestation from the system owner explaining why an export cannot be produced.
- SOC 2 bridge: do you have a current SOC 2 report or an SOC 2 readiness memo? That will accelerate testing where controls overlap.

Attached is Acme’s standard intake form — fill the top-level fields and return to security-intake so we can route to the auditor with minimal back-and-forth.

Regards,
Clara Holt
Head of Vendor Assurance
Acme Financial

Attachment: Acme_audit_request_form.pdf (PDF stub; please complete section A-C)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Clara Holt <clara@acme-fin.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Jan 2028 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Control sampling & evidence prioritization — decision request (final)

Clara / team —

Thanks — we’ll do the following and get you the artifacts & metadata by Jan 27 EOD: 

1) Scope: Dedicated clusters only. I’ll send a separate email listing cluster IDs and agent/service versions by EOD Jan 24 (Jonas is collecting).
2) Sampling windows: provide 90-day exports for operational logs + 12-month exports for change-control/config artifacts where available. Where 12 months is not available we’ll provide an attestation and the available retention history.
3) Evidence formats: CSV/JSON exports preferred. Screenshots only if export unavailable; owner-signed attestation required.
4) Sampling counts: risk-weighted as Marissa recommended (5 high, 3 medium, 1 low). For FedRAMP-mapped high controls target n=7 where feasible.

Action owners & deadlines:
- Jonas Weber: send cluster IDs, agent versions, and populate evidence_index_template.csv (due Jan 24, 5pm PT).
- Olga Petrov: confirm KMS and key rotation artifacts and owners; upload sample exports to the shared drive (due Jan 26).
- Marissa Cole: attach ISO->FedRAMP->Internal control mapping to the sheet and draft a short SOC 2 readiness note (due Jan 26).
- Me: send auditor reply and upload initial packet to the drive (Jan 27).

Links: evidence folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-evidence), HubSpot deal (https://hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2028-4893).

If auditors need a different minimal n per control, we’ll adjust after receipt of that guidance. Otherwise we’ll proceed with the plan above.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Director, Security & Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
